learning_objective: 🎯 Explore how villages run their own local magic called the Panchayati Raj, making sure everyone has a voice in solving problems!

main_concepts.concept_title: 🌱 Power at the Roots: Grassroots Democracy
main_concepts.simple_explanation: Grassroots means at the ground level! Instead of a big boss far away making all the rules, grassroots democracy lets the local people in a village decide what is best for their own homes.
In Indian villages, adults vote to choose a group of leaders called the Gram Panchayat. These leaders meet under trees or in halls to fix roads, arrange clean water, and build schools.

main_concepts.concept_title: 👳‍♂️ The Captain of the Village: The Sarpanch
main_concepts.simple_explanation: The head or the captain of the Gram Panchayat is called the Sarpanch. Along with the other members (Panchas), the Sarpanch listens to the villagers' problems and finds fair solutions.

fun_activity.title: ⚖️ The Family Panchayat
fun_activity.instructions: Hold a mock Panchayat meeting at home! Elect someone as the Sarpanch, gather everyone in a circle, and discuss a 'village' problem, like what to cook for dinner or how to keep the living room clean.

quick_recap: ⭐ Grassroots democracy means giving decision-making power directly to local people.
⭐ The Gram Panchayat is the local government that looks after the needs of a village.
⭐ The Sarpanch is the elected head of the Panchayat who helps solve local issues.
